::: callout-warning
Sail support is experimental. It is only available in the development
version of `pysparklyr`.

``` r
pak::pak("mlverse/pysparklyr")
```
:::

## Intro

[Sail](https://github.com/lakehq/sail) is a Spark Connect server written
in Rust. It does not need Java or a JVM. Sail runs the same Spark
DataFrame and SQL commands that Spark does, so `sparklyr` can talk to it
the same way it talks to [Spark Connect](/deployment/spark-connect.qmd). You
can connect to a remote Sail server that is already running, or to
a local Sail server on your machine.

## Get started

To start and work with a local Sail server, use `"sail"` as the `method`.
If you can use [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) on your machine,
`sparklyr` installs the Python libraries that Sail needs when you
connect. It then starts a local Sail server and connects you to it. You
do not need to do any other setup (a.k.a. **no Java needed!**).


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(sparklyr)

sc <- spark_connect(master = "local", method = "sail")
#> Retrieving version from PyPi.org
#> ✔ PyPi specs: 'pyspark-client' version 4.2.0, requires Python >=3.10 [52ms]
#> 
#> ℹ
#> ✔ Python environment: 'Managed `uv` environment' [558ms]
#> 
```
:::


The server uses a free port on your machine. `spark_disconnect()` stops
the server. The server also stops when the R session ends.

## Python environment

If you cannot use `uv`, run `install_sail()` once, before you connect.
It creates a Python environment that stays on your machine. These are
the main libraries in the new Python environment:

-   `pyspark-client`, which is a thin version of `pyspark`
-   `pysail`, which `sparklyr` uses to start local Sail servers
-   `rpy2`, which runs the R code that `spark_apply()` sends

``` r
pysparklyr::install_sail()
```

To install a specific Sail version, pass it in `version`:

``` r
pysparklyr::install_sail(version = "0.7")
```

After that, connect with `spark_connect()` as shown in [Get
started](#get-started). `sparklyr` finds and uses the new environment.

## How it works

`sparklyr` uses `reticulate` to call the Python `pyspark-client`
library. That library sends the commands to the Sail server over
*gRPC*. With a "local" connection, the Sail server runs inside your R
session.

## Work with data

Sail does not cache tables in memory, so set `memory` to `FALSE`:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(dplyr)

mtcars_tbl <- copy_to(sc, mtcars, memory = FALSE, overwrite = TRUE)

mtcars_tbl |>
  group_by(am) |>
  summarise(mpg = mean(mpg, na.rm = TRUE))
#> # A query:  ?? x 2
#> # Database: connect_sail
#>      am   mpg
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1  24.4
#> 2     0  17.1
```
:::


## Run R code

`spark_apply()` runs R code against each part of the data:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mtcars_tbl |>
  spark_apply(nrow, group_by = "am", columns = "am double, x long")
#> # A query:  ?? x 2
#> # Database: connect_sail
#>      am     x
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1    13
#> 2     0    19
```
:::


With a "local" connection, the R code runs inside your R session, not
in a separate R process. This means:

-   If the R code crashes, it can end your R session
-   The R code can change objects in your global environment


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
spark_disconnect(sc)
```
:::


## Connect to a running Sail server

You can also connect to a Sail server that is already running. Pass the
server's address in `master`. The address uses the "sc://" protocol:

``` r
sc <- spark_connect(
  master = "sc://localhost:50051",
  method = "sail"
)
```

The Python environment of the server needs `pyspark-client`. To use
`spark_apply()`, the server also needs:

-   `rpy2`
-   R
-   The same Python version as your R session

See the [Sail
documentation](https://docs.lakesail.com/sail/latest/) to learn how to
start a Sail server.

## Limitations

Sail does not support some `sparklyr` features:

-   **Caching** - `copy_to()` and the `spark_read_*()` functions need
    `memory = FALSE`. `compute()` returns an error.
-   **Machine learning** - The `ml_*()` and `ft_*()` functions do not
    work.
-   **Tuning** - `tune_grid_spark()` does not work.
